Have a Gross Monthly Household Income of <= S$15,000 at the point of admission (GMHI is the total monthly income received by working members of the household from employment and business, including basic employment income, trade/self-employed income, overtime pay, allowances, cash awards, commissions, or bonuses)

official.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship is awarded to exceptional polytechnic graduates who demonstrate academic excellence, outstanding extracurricular involvement, and a strong passion for STEM fields, enabling them to pursue further education at top overseas universities and contribute to Singapore's innovation and growth upon graduation. It is part of Temasek's T-Spring community gift announced in June 2024 to mark Temasek's 50th anniversary, which aims to advance capabilities for a future-ready workforce in Singapore.

applicant_utility.summary: This is full funding for Singapore Citizen polytechnic graduates reading a STEM degree (not Medicine or Dentistry) at a top overseas university: Temasek covers tuition and compulsory fees for the whole course, pays a monthly living allowance, adds one-off relocation and pre-studies allowances, and reimburses up to five university application fees plus visa fees - but it publishes no monetary figures, so plan around benefit categories rather than numbers. The AY2026/2027 window closed on 15 September 2026, so expect the next cycle around the same July-September pattern and check the official page instead of trusting the stale 'now open' banner. Selection runs four stages - psychometric tests, an on-demand video interview, a one-day group assessment and a 60-minute final interview - so decisions take weeks, and graduation triggers a 4-year STEM bond in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong final-year or recent local polytechnic graduates with a STEM diploma, a solid co-curricular record and household income of S$15,000 a month or less, who want a fully funded overseas bachelor's and accept a 4-year STEM bond back home.
application_readiness_checklist: Build ONE consolidated file early: GCE O-level and polytechnic diploma certificates, pre-tertiary results, CCA records and prizes, plus any university offers - the portal uploads it under CV submission
Recompute household income on Temasek's broad GMHI definition (overtime, allowances, commissions, cash awards and self-employed trade income all count) before assuming you clear the S$15,000 cap
Start overseas university applications in parallel, because acceptance at an overseas university is needed to confirm even a provisional offer
Diarise the four-stage funnel - online psychometric and personality test, remote on-demand video interview, one-day in-person group assessment, 60-minute final interview - and keep those days free
Re-check the official Temasek page before the window opens; the AY2026/2027 text was still advertising the window after its 15 September 2026 closing date
common_rejection_risks: Household income above S$15,000 a month when measured at the point of admission using the broad GMHI definition
Applying for Medicine or Dentistry, or a non-STEM course - both are explicitly excluded
Non-citizens applying: despite the overseas destination, the award is restricted to Singapore citizens
Scattered uploads instead of the mandated single consolidated file, so assessors never see the certificates
Assuming the live banner means the current round is still accepting applications and missing the next window
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Temasek publishes no amounts, so anything beyond the listed categories - university application fees beyond five institutions, living costs above the monthly allowance, and all personal spending - is borne by the scholar.
document_audit: Everything must sit in one consolidated file uploaded under CV submission; certificates sent separately or pasted into the form body risk never being seen
Preliminary polytechnic results are accepted while finals are pending, but the provisional offer only firms up once final cumulative GPA, examination results and an overseas acceptance are released
University application and outcomes are requested 'if available' - apply to universities early enough that this section is not empty by submission time
alerts: The official page still shows the AY2026/2027 window as open although it closed on 15 September 2026 - do not assume the current round is live
The S$15,000 Gross Monthly Household Income ceiling is tested at the point of admission, not at application
Medicine and Dentistry are explicitly excluded from an otherwise STEM-wide eligibility
Graduation carries a 4-year bond in a STEM-related role in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the 'Apply Now via Brightsparks' button on the official page, upload the single consolidated document file under CV submission with the GMHI declaration, then progress through the shortlisting stages if contacted.
